summary: Incremental SIEM export: adaptive sampling, schema-version header, and GDPR deletion propagation proof
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a formal mechanism and proof for three things related to their live SIEM export to an on-prem Kafka cluster: (1) support for adaptive (per-tenant) sampling in the incremental export so high-volume tenants are sampled at route-time, (2) a schema-version header in every export message and manifest so downstream parsers can tolerate rolling changes, and (3) verifiable propagation of GDPR deletion requests into the export stream (i.e., when an end-user is erased, no subsequent SIEM export should contain their events).

Impact:
PulsePay is using Redwood's tenant-scoped incremental SIEM feed for fraud telemetry ingestion. They discovered during a data-protection validation that (a) sampled test slices still contained events for deleted user ids, and (b) consumer parsing logic lacks a stable schema version to guard against producer changes. This prevents them from signing off on production onboarding and is blocking final contract acceptance.

Environment:
- Customer environment: enterprise account (PulsePay Financial)
- Export target: on-prem Kafka cluster (TLS mTLS) via the Redwood SIEM Bridge connector
- Redwood environment: prod-us-east incremental-export pipeline v2.4.1

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Submit a GDPR deletion request for user id: usr_9b2fc1 via self-service API.
2) Observe that deletion job returns success and user disappears from console.
3) Wait for next incremental export window (15-minute cadence).
4) Consumer shows events with the deleted user id in the exported Kafka topic between offsets 120304-120420.

Customer-provided logs/snippets:
- Example exported event (sanitized): {"ts":"2026-03-09T18:12:03Z", "user_id": "usr_9b2fc1", "event_type": "prompt_submit", "tenant_id": "pp-prod"}
- Bridge connector config: sampling_policy=adaptive_per_tenant, sampling_rate_overrides=[pp-prod:0.01], include_headers=false

Requested deliverables:
- A reproducible explanation for how deletion/tombstone propagation is handled by the incremental-export pipeline and why the customer observed post-deletion events.
- A short-term workaround the customer can enable to avoid leaked deletion events while we implement a longer-term solution.
- A timeline and PRs for adding an explicit X-Schema-Version header to export messages and a manifest file for each export window.
- Signed manifest or attestation proving previously exported windows were scanned for deleted ids (optional but strongly requested).

Additional notes from customer:
They prefer minimal downtime and would accept an opt-in config flag to make deletion propagation immediate even if it increases export latency for a subset of tenants.
comments: Priya Nair (Support): Received at 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC. Acknowledged and triaged to integration/SIEM team. Assigned to Marcus.

Marcus Bell (Eng): 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC - Reproduced locally using a staging mirror of the customer's Kafka topic. Preliminary signal: tombstone markers are created but there is a 1-export-window retention buffer in the exporter staging queue which can cause deleted events to be shipped if they were buffered before tombstone propagation completed.

PulsePay Contact (Ella Rodriguez): 2026-03-10 14:20 UTC - We observed two exported events after deletion but they had offsets within the same minute the deletion was submitted. We need a guarantee that this cannot recur for PCI/PD compliance.

Marcus Bell (Eng): 2026-03-11 08:34 UTC - Filing for short-term mitigation: enable immediate-tombstone-propagation flag for pp-prod and reduce export window to 1 minute for their tenant. Will coordinate with infra to run backfill scan and provide signed manifest for last 24h.
Security (Lina Chen): 2026-03-11 10:02 UTC - For attestation, we'll produce an HMAC manifest signed with the enterprise key and include a per-window checksum. Draft PR linked in ticket.

Marcus Bell (Eng): 2026-03-12 16:41 UTC - Patch landed to add X-Schema-Version header and manifest generation; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9854. Scheduling deploy to prod-us-east on 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC behind a feature flag.
investigation_notes: Confirmed reproduction against customer's staging mirror; exporter has two internal buffers: ingest-buffer (where sampling is applied) and dispatch-window buffer. Tombstone propagation currently flows to ingest-buffer but dispatch-window flush can contain pre-tombstone events.

Sampling: adaptive_per_tenant logic was working, but header-less exports made downstream dedup and suppression rules brittle. The sampling algorithm marks events with internal _sampling_version but not emitted in headers; we'll expose a public header X-Sampling-Version as part of schema changes.

Root cause for leaked deletions: exporter dispatch-window buffer size + asynchronous tombstone propagation. If an event is buffered and the deletion request arrives after buffering but before dispatch, the deletion marker is applied only to new events, not already buffered ones.
Risk assessment: This is a correctness/regulatory risk for enterprise customers with short-deletion SLAs. Low probability at scale but high impact for affected tenants.

Mitigation options considered: (A) immediate-tombstone-propagation (sync) per-tenant; (B) reduce dispatch window to 1 minute for opt-in tenants; (C) post-export backfill scan that removes/marks records and emits compensating deletions to downstream systems. Recommended: short-term (B) + backfill; long-term (A) with metrics and canary rollouts.
resolution: Short-term workaround: Enabled immediate-tombstone-propagation and reduced export window to 1 minute for tenant pp-prod for PulsePay. Coordinates: infra runbook step executed 2026-03-11 18:10 UTC.

Backfill: Ran a 24-hour backfill scan against the exported topics and produced a signed HMAC manifest (SHA256) of removed offsets. Manifest S3 path: s3://redwood-evidence/pulsepay/pp-prod/backfill/2026-03-11-manifest.json (access granted to PulsePay via presigned URL).

Schema/versioning: X-Schema-Version and X-Sampling-Version headers added to exporter messages and manifest generation implemented. PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9854. Deploy scheduled behind feature flag 2026-03-14.

Long-term plan: Implement immediate-tombstone-propagation as configurable default for enterprise tier with telemetry and per-tenant latency impact telemetry. Track as follow-up work: INT-4107 (engineering work item for permanent change).

Customer acceptance: PulsePay validated the backfill manifest and confirmed they no longer observed deleted user ids in the reprocessed topic. They requested a short runbook for how to request immediate-tombstone-propagation for other tenants; Support to provide template.
final_notes: Next steps: 1) Deploy schema/manifest feature to prod-us-east behind flag on 2026-03-14 and coordinate a canary rollout with PulsePay. 2) Create a short runbook for customers to request immediate-tombstone-propagation and include expected cost/latency tradeoffs. 3) Close ticket once PulsePay signs off on the feature and receives the formal attestation artifact. Ticket owner: Marcus Bell.
